title: A fourth in the fire (Daniel 3)
hook: three young men refuse to bow and walk unharmed in the furnace

segments.voice: Yesterday, Daniel purposed in his heart and asked for pulse and water instead of the king's food. Today, his three friends face something hotter than a menu.

The band is the signal. On the plain of Dura, King Nebuchadnezzar has set up a great image of gold and called every official in the land before it. A herald gives the rule: when you hear the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer and every kind of music, fall down and worship the golden image. Whoever doesn't goes into a burning fiery furnace. The music starts. The whole plain goes down. Three men don't: Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, the friends from yesterday. Someone reports them, and the king, in a rage, gives them one more chance.
screen: `A GOLDEN IMAGE ON THE PLAIN.` → `THE MUSIC IS THE SIGNAL.` → `THREE MEN DON'T BOW.`

segments.voice: Their answer turns on three small words. In the King James words: "If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up." But if not. They don't bargain. They don't say, we'll stand because we know we'll be rescued. They say God is able, and even if no rescue comes, the answer is still no. The furnace is heated seven times hotter than usual; the men who throw them in are killed by the heat. Then the king jumps up, astonished. He counts. "Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt." Four. The fourth, he says, looks like a son of the gods. Later the king himself says their God sent his angel. They went in bound. Now they walk loose. When they come out, the text lists what isn't there: not a hair singed, their coats unchanged, not even the smell of fire on them. The story doesn't say the fire wasn't real. It says they weren't alone in it.
screen: then, large: `ABLE TO DELIVER US. BUT IF NOT.` · `FOUR MEN LOOSE IN THE FIRE.` · `THEY WENT IN BOUND. NOW THEY WALK LOOSE.` · then: `NOT EVEN THE SMELL OF FIRE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one thing you've decided is right and mean to keep doing: a promise, a line you hold at work, a way of telling the truth. Say what you hope will come of it, then the other half, but if not, and ask whether you'd still do it with the happy ending taken away. If you pray, ask in words from your tradition not to be alone in it.
If not. The three words the friends anchor their answer on: God is able, but if not, the answer is still no. Today's word.
Your line: not alone in the fire. God is able, but if not, the answer is still no. That's day eight hundred seventy.

howItsDone: Jewish teachers tell the story of Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, the Hebrew names of Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, as an example of refusing to worship an idol even at great risk.

chat.meaning: Their answer: God is able to deliver us, but if not, we will not serve thy gods. No bargain, just the answer.

Dura.meaning: the plain where Nebuchadnezzar set up the golden image

Shadrach.meaning: Hananiah's Babylonian name; one of Daniel's three friends

Meshach.meaning: Mishael's Babylonian name; one of Daniel's three friends

Abed-nego.meaning: Azariah's Babylonian name; the third of Daniel's friends

Nebuchadnezzar.meaning: the king of Babylon who set up the golden image

notes: Daniel 3:25 ends differently in translations: the KJV has 'like the Son of God', JPS 1917 'like a son of the gods'. The script paraphrases as 'a son of the gods' and quotes only the shared first half; Keeper please confirm this is right for the Jewish path.
Daniel 3:18 is in Aramaic (Daniel 2:4b–7:28); the original game says 'this chapter' is Aramaic. Please verify the pointing of וְהֵן לָא.
